description: A pair of oscillators whose waves come from the formula n to the power of x over n to the power of x plus one, counted out sample by sample

params.text: Sets the pitch in whole octaves, three either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the first exponent, from 0.01 to 2; small values give a nearly flat wave and large ones a sharper corner
Sets the second exponent, from -0.01 to -2, which turns the curve the other way up

inputs.text: Adds to the pitch, an octave per volt, with the total held within four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Adds to the first exponent, a fifth per volt, with nothing clamping the total
Adds to the second exponent, a fifth per volt in the negative direction, with nothing clamping the total

outputs.text: The first wave, a rising curve whose bend is set by POW 1, reset at the start of every cycle
The second wave, a rising curve whose bend is set by POW 2, reset at the start of every cycle

notes: the cycle length is a whole number of samples, so the pitch is only as accurate as that rounding allows and is coarse at high frequencies.
the second wave is built with a different offset and gain from the first, so it is louder and carries a DC offset; both are clamped at ±5V.
the exponent CV jacks are not clamped, so a large voltage can push an exponent past the ends of its knob and out of the useful range.

inputs.0: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
